sources.title: Job
sources.notes: CAFC job-scam page (seen in search results; direct fetch blocked in research environment, content from search summary). Covers money-mule 'payment processor' jobs, counterfeit cheques, task/'boosting' jobs that demand crypto deposits, and fake online-store/survey jobs.
tips: Never send a deposit or pay 'upgrade' or 'unlock' fees to get work
Do not receive and forward money through your bank account for an employer
A cheque you must cash and partly send back is a scam
Task 'boosting' jobs that show earnings then ask you to pay in are scams
Report job scams to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre

sources.title: Money mule awareness
sources.notes: CAFC feature on money mules (search result; not opened). Job titles such as 'financial agent' or 'client manager' can hide money-laundering schemes.
tips: Be wary of 'financial agent', 'payment processor' or 'client manager' job offers
Moving money for others can expose you to money-laundering charges

sources.title: Top 10 frauds in 2025
sources.notes: February 2026 CAFC feature (search result; not opened). CAFC search results reported 2,148 job fraud reports, 1,726 victims and $50.6M in losses in 2025, with job fraud among the top three by financial impact; exact page for these figures not confirmed.
tips: Job fraud is one of the costliest frauds in Canada, so verify any offer before sharing money or ID

sources.title: Job and employment scams - Competition Bureau Canada
sources.notes: Official Bureau tips page (search result; not opened). Warns about guaranteed high income for little effort, upfront fees for business plans/start-up kits/software, using your bank account to pass payments, and fake-cheque overpayment schemes.
tips: Be suspicious of jobs that guarantee high income for little effort
Never pay upfront for a 'business plan', start-up kit or software to get work
No legitimate business sends you a cheque and asks you to transfer part back
Research offers independently and get advice before agreeing
Do not give banking or card details to people you do not know and trust

sources.title: Job Search Safety Tips - Job Bank
sources.notes: Official Job Bank safety page (search result; not opened). Advice on protecting personal information, reporting suspicious postings and immigration-related email scams.
tips: Legitimate employers will not ask for banking information to apply
Keep your SIN, birth date and licence or health card numbers off your resume and out of early interviews
Use 'Report a problem with this job posting' on Job Bank if something looks wrong
Job Bank does not handle immigration; distrust emails offering immigration services in its name
Look for the 'Posted on Job Bank' flag on postings created by registered employers

sources.title: O. Reg. 99/23: Licensing - Temporary Help Agencies and Recruiters, Employment Standards Act, 2000
sources.notes: Ontario regulation requiring temp help agencies and recruiters to be licensed (search result; not opened). Fee prohibition for workers reported by secondary sources (Parkdale Community Legal Services, Canadian HR Reporter), not confirmed on an ontario.ca guide page.
tips: In Ontario, temp help agencies and recruiters must hold a licence
Ontario temp agencies may not charge workers a fee to be hired or assigned work (per legal-clinic and HR press reports)
